title: Social Housing Purchase Conditions 2026: Eligibility and Income
desc: Who can buy social housing in 2026: 12 eligible groups, no home or under 15 m² per person, income of no more than VND 25, 35 or 50 million per month.
summary: A summary of eligible groups, housing conditions and maximum income levels for buying or lease-purchasing social housing under the Housing Law 2023 and Decree 136/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

Social housing is priced lower than commercial housing, so it is reserved for people who meet all conditions on eligible group, housing and income. This article summarises the rules under Housing Law No. 27/2023/QH15 and Decree 100/2024/ND-CP as amended, most recently by Decree 136/2026/ND-CP (effective 7 April 2026).
h2
1. Who is eligible for social housing support?
p
Under Article 76 of the Housing Law, there are 12 eligible groups. The groups entitled to buy or lease-purchase social housing (Clause 1, Article 77) include:
ul
People with meritorious services to the revolution and relatives of martyrs who qualify for housing improvement support.
Poor and near-poor households in urban areas.
Low-income earners in urban areas.
Workers and employees working at enterprises, cooperatives and cooperative unions, inside and outside industrial parks.
Officers, professional soldiers, non-commissioned officers and police workers... who have not yet benefited from housing policies for the armed forces.
Cadres, civil servants and public employees.

People who have returned official housing (except where it was recovered due to violations); households and individuals whose land was reclaimed and houses demolished but who have not been compensated with housing or residential land.
p
Poor and near-poor households in rural areas may buy if the provincial People's Committee so provides; students and pupils may only rent during their period of study.
h2
2. Housing conditions
p
Under Point a, Clause 1, Article 78 and Article 29 of Decree 100/2024/ND-CP, the buyer must fall into one of two cases in the province or city where the project is located:
ul

No home: the applicant and their spouse (if any) are not named on a Certificate in that province or city at the time of filing; and have not bought or lease-purchased social housing nor received housing support policies in any form there.
A home but too cramped: the average housing area is under 15 m² of floor area per person, counted for the applicant, spouse, parents and children registered as permanent residents at that house.
h2
3. Income conditions (applicable from 7 April 2026)
p

For low-income earners in urban areas, workers and employees, and cadres, civil servants and public employees, Article 1 of Decree 136/2026/ND-CP provides that average monthly take-home income must not exceed:
ul
VND 25 million if the applicant is unmarried or certified as single.
VND 35 million if single and raising a child under 18.
VND 50 million combined income of the two spouses if married.
p

Income is calculated over the 12 consecutive months before the date the competent authority certifies it, based on wage and salary statements certified by the workplace. The provincial People's Committee may decide an adjustment coefficient for the income level according to local conditions. For low-income urban residents without a labour contract, the commune-level Police of the place of permanent residence, temporary residence or current residence certifies the income within 7 days (Clause 2, Article 30 as amended by Decree 261/2025/ND-CP). The armed forces apply a separate level calculated on the income of an officer at the rank of Colonel.
p
Income certifications issued under the old rules before 7 April 2026 remain usable for 12 months from the date of certification (Article 2 of Decree 136/2026/ND-CP).
h2
4. How many units can you buy, and when can you resell?
ul
Each eligible person may buy or lease-purchase only 1 unit of social housing (Clause 6, Article 88).

The first advance payment is no more than 30% of the contract value (including the deposit); total payments are no more than 70% before handover and no more than 95% before the Certificate is issued (Point c, Clause 1, Article 89).

Within 5 years of full payment, the unit may be resold only to the investor or to a person eligible to buy social housing, at a price no higher than the original purchase price; after 5 years and once a Certificate has been issued, it may be sold at the market price.
Buying by an ineligible person or without meeting the conditions makes the contract void and the unit must be returned (Clause 10, Article 88).
h2
5. Where to submit the application
p

Interested persons follow project information published on the website of the Department of Construction, then submit the dossier directly to the investor. The dossier consists of an application form and documents proving eligibility and conditions, using the forms of the Ministry of Construction (Article 38 of Decree 100/2024/ND-CP; Circular 32/2025/TT-BXD). If married, the spouse must also declare income documents.
p
To learn more about buying a home before the project is completed, see Buying Off-Plan Housing 2026.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. Decree 100/2024/ND-CP has been amended several times (Decrees 261/2025, 54/2026 and 136/2026); our library does not yet include Decree 54/2026/ND-CP. Some articles still refer to "district-level" authority under the former government model. Before submitting a dossier, ask the Department of Construction where the project is located about the income level and adjustment coefficient currently applied.
